questions.question: Why is a numeric 3D position incomplete without a coordinate frame and timestamp?
options: The same numbers can describe different places or moments in device, map, anchor, or world space
Frames only determine texture compression
Timestamps are needed only for cloud billing
All spatial runtimes use one immutable global coordinate system
questions.explanation: Spatial meaning depends on both the reference frame and the time at which the pose or transform was valid.

questions.question: A 90 fps target gives approximately how much time per frame?
options: 5.6 ms
8.3 ms
questions.explanation: One second divided by 90 frames is about 11.1 milliseconds per frame.

questions.question: Where should a 55 ms cloud inference normally sit in a head-tracked rendering architecture?
options: On the blocking pose-to-display path
As an asynchronous, versioned update to a future frame with a local fallback
Between the renderer and display scanout
Inside the IMU interrupt handler
questions.explanation: Remote semantics can enrich later frames, but blocking the live frame path would miss a typical immersive display deadline.

questions.question: What should world-locked application behavior do when tracking confidence is lost?
options: Keep presenting exact placement from the last pose indefinitely
Move authority to the cloud automatically
Pause high-impact spatial actions and show body-locked recovery guidance
Delete every persisted anchor
questions.explanation: A runtime should expose uncertainty and fall back safely rather than fabricate a precise world transform.

questions.question: Why is loading a persisted anchor identifier not enough to render content immediately?
options: The current session must still localize that anchor and establish a confident transform
Anchor identifiers contain the complete current room mesh
Persistence guarantees the physical environment never changes
Persisted anchors can only support body-locked content
questions.explanation: Durable identity does not prove that the current sensor map can locate the anchor or that the environment still matches.

questions.question: Which fields make an asynchronous semantic result safer to apply?
options: Only the label text
Map, anchor, entity, capture-time, and model versions plus confidence
A global average latency
The user interface color theme
questions.explanation: Version and freshness checks prevent a late result from being applied to a different map, entity state, or model contract.

questions.question: Two participants move one shared spatial entity concurrently. What must the application define?
options: A deterministic ownership or conflict policy and frame-rebasing behavior
A higher display brightness
A single network retry count
A larger texture atlas
questions.explanation: Delivery alone cannot decide physical authority; the collaboration model must resolve operation order and transform the result into each local frame.
